bull.b: Consistent, substantial free cash flow (2026 FCF ~616M and strong cash conversion) creates durable financial flexibility. It funds capex, buybacks, deleveraging and acquisitions without relying on external financing, insulating the business through cycles and supporting reinvestment.

Growing ARR and a sizeable RPO backlog boost revenue visibility and stickiness. A >$2B ARR and rapidly expanding RPO mean repeatable consumables and services revenue, reducing cyclicality, improving predictability of cash flows and supporting long-term margin expansion from subscription mix.

Material deleveraging since 2022 yields a healthier capital structure and larger equity base, lowering financial risk. The stronger balance sheet increases capacity for strategic investments, M&A, supply-chain resilience and continued shareholder returns without materially raising solvency risk.

bear.b: Unprecedented memory/NAND inflation is a structural margin headwind until input costs normalize or pricing fully adjusts. Prolonged cost pressure can compress product gross margins, shorten quote windows, increase operational complexity and force customer pull-ins that distort demand timing.

A large portion of anticipated upside is concentrated in H2 from hyperscaler shipments. This timing concentration raises execution and visibility risk: delays or slower ramp could materially affect full-year results and makes near-term forecasting and resource allocation more uncertain.

While gross margins are strong, operating margins remain modest relative to revenue scale, indicating limited operating leverage or elevated operating costs. Sustained margin compression would constrain reinvestment, limit cash available for returns and increase reliance on volume growth for profit expansion.
